answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before it may submit bids, with larger bonds for actions that expose others to greater risk. A Sybil attacker can still create many keys, but each one ties up real capital; splitting a fixed budget among them also leaves each identity with less influence. Bonds are forfeited when a challenge proves fraud, while honest agents recover them, so copying names is cheap but buying durable participation is not. Even a lagoon timber market can set bond size with the tide of recent fraud losses.
